We are a leading global manufacturer and marketer of branded consumer foods with more than 100 brands in 100 countries across six continents. In addition to our consolidated operations, we have 50 percent interests in two strategic joint ventures that manufacture and market food products sold in approximately 120 countries worldwide. We manage and review the financial results of our business under four operating segments: North America Retail; International; North America Pet; and North America Foodservice. See Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) in Item 7 of this report for a description of our segments. We offer a variety of human and pet food products that provide great taste, nutrition, convenience, and value for consumers around the world. Our business is focused on the following large, global categories: • snacks, including grain, fruit and savory snacks, nutrition bars, and frozen hot snacks; • ready-to-eat cereal; • convenient meals, including meal kits, ethnic meals, pizza, soup, side dish mixes, frozen breakfast, and frozen entrees; • wholesome natural pet food; • refrigerated and frozen dough; • baking mixes and ingredients; and • super-premium ice cream. Our Cereal Partners Worldwide (CPW) joint venture with Nestlé S.A. (Nestlé) competes in the ready-to-eat cereal category in markets outside North America, and our Häagen-Dazs Japan, Inc. (HDJ) joint venture competes in the super-premium ice cream category in Japan. For net sales contributed by each class of similar products, please see Note 17 to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report. credit_strengths.text: General Mills' branded portfolio across snacks, cereal, convenient meals and pet food, spanning four operating segments and two strategic joint ventures, underpins repeat-purchase demand and pricing power that support the revenue base despite the disclosed decline in net sales.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure and dividends combined, and covers dividends alone with headroom, indicating the core grocery business still generates cash sufficient to fund the stated distribution policy from operations rather than borrowing.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits far above the sector median and has risen sharply year on year, placing the issuer in the weakest indicative leverage band; the disclosed operating income decline against a stable debt balance drives most of the deterioration rather than new borrowing.

The debt note shows refinancing activity concentrated in near-dated maturities, with junior subordinated notes issued to repay senior notes and commercial paper; the reset-rate structure on those subordinated notes introduces future coupon step-up risk at each reset date.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage has fallen well below the sector median and below the prior year, reflecting compressed operating income against a cash interest burden that now absorbs a large share of earnings; coverage remains above one but with thin cushion against further margin erosion.

Free cash flow to debt is below the sector median and weaker year on year, and free cash flow falls short of combined dividends and buybacks, so shareholder returns are partly funded from balance sheet capacity rather than internally generated cash alone.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is highly leveraged, with leverage and cash-flow coverage both materially weaker than Consumer Staples peers; the current ratio also sits below the sector median and below one, indicating reliance on refinancing short-term obligations.

Our judgement is that the credit depends on restoring operating margin toward prior levels; absent that, distributions exceeding free cash flow and the subordinated note reset schedule would keep leverage elevated, and the disclosed cash interest proxy is the key sensitivity for coverage.

credit_strengths.text: 通用磨坊橫跨零食、穀物、方便餐及寵物食品的品牌組合，涵蓋四個營運分部及兩家策略合資企業，支撐重複購買需求及定價能力，儘管披露的淨銷售額下降，仍支持收入基礎。
營運現金流足以從容覆蓋資本開支與股息之總和，且單獨覆蓋股息仍有餘裕，顯示核心雜貨業務仍產生足夠現金，可從營運而非借貸為所述分派政策提供資金。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿遠高於行業中位數，且按年大幅上升，使發行人處於最弱的指示性槓桿區間；披露的營運收入下降而債務結餘穩定，是大部分惡化的主因，而非新增借貸。
債務附註顯示再融資活動集中於近期到期債務，並發行次級後償票據以償還優先票據及商業票據；該等次級票據的重設利率結構，在每個重設日期引入未來票息遞增風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率已遠低於行業中位數及低於上一年，反映營運收入受壓，而現金利息負擔現時佔盈利一大部分；覆蓋率仍高於一，但對進一步利潤率侵蝕的緩衝薄弱。
自由現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數且按年轉弱，而自由現金流不足以覆蓋股息與回購之總和，故股東回報部分由資產負債表能力而非僅內部產生現金提供資金。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為高槓桿，槓桿及現金流覆蓋均顯著弱於消費必需品同業；流動比率亦低於行業中位數及低於一，顯示依賴再融資短期債務。
我們的判斷是，該信貸取決於營運利潤率能否恢復至先前水平；若未能如此，超出自由現金流的分派及次級票據重設時間表將使槓桿維持高企，而披露的現金利息代理指標是覆蓋率的關鍵敏感因素。
